summary.short: Mexico's General Population Law as amended on 16 July 2025: makes the national identity key (CURP) a mandatory universal identity document that may include biometric data, requires public and private entities to request it for procedures, and sets fines for non-compliance with biometric integration duties.
summary.long: Consolidated text of the Ley General de Población, last reformed DOF 16-07-2025. The 2025 decree adds Arts. 91 Bis to 91 Sexies and 114 Bis. Art. 91 Bis makes the Clave Única de Registro de Población (CURP) a mandatory national identity document, universally accepted, that may also contain fingerprints and a photograph, in physical and digital form. The Secretaría de Gobernación must integrate biometric data into the CURP by transfer from authorities of the three levels of government or by attendance at enabling centres, and integration requires the holders' prior consent. Art. 91 Ter links the biometric CURP to the National Health System Registry. Art. 91 Quater creates a single identity platform within the National Population Registry. Art. 91 Quinquies assigns the digital CURP to the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones. Art. 91 Sexies requires use of the CURP for digital identity validation and obliges all public and private entities to request it for their procedures and services. Art. 114 Bis sets fines of 10,000 to 20,000 times the daily Unidad de Medida y Actualización for authorities and private parties that repeatedly fail to meet Art. 91 Bis duties, after prior warning. Transitory provisions set 90-day and 120-day deadlines for the platform, consent mechanisms, the CURP requirement and a biometric programme for children and adolescents.

notes: Text is the consolidated Ley General de Población, Última Reforma DOF 16-07-2025. The registry title names the 2025 decree that added art. 91 (second paragraph), arts 91 Bis to 91 Sexies and art. 114 Bis. Relations follow the reform history in the text and are not an article-level record of every change. Internal points: art. 10 is marked derogated (DOF 25-05-2011) and re-added by DOF 09-04-2012 (text note). Arts 7 to 75 and fractions VII and VIII of art. 3 are marked derogated 25-05-2011, but the 2011 decree's Transitorio Segundo makes those derogations effective only once the Reglamento de la Ley de Migración is in force.
